title: Fetcher: rewrite disk parsing for Hardware.Storage.Details nvme/sata/hdd arrays
description:
_parse_disks in pipeline/src/pipeline/fetcher.py currently expects a flat disks/storage/drives list or legacy hdd_count/hdd_size_gb fields -- none of which exist in the real feed. Full schema + worked example in docs/notes/hetzner-live-feed-schema-2026-08-06.md.

Real shape: item['Hardware']['Storage']['Details'] is a dict with keys hdd, sata, nvme (each a flat list of per-disk capacity-in-GB integers, one entry per physical disk) plus a redundant general key (ignore it -- it's a flattened union of the other three, not a fourth type).

Rewrite _parse_disks to:
- Map hdd->"HDD", sata->"SSD" (Hetzner's SATA auction drives are SSDs, not spinning disks -- confirmed against Details.Information's human-readable strings), nvme->"NVMe".
- Group each type's flat capacity list into DiskSpec(type, count, capacity_gb) by identical capacity value -- e.g. hdd:[6000,6000] -> one DiskSpec(HDD, count=2, capacity_gb=6000). A type with differing capacities (e.g. sata:[500,250]) emits one DiskSpec per distinct capacity -- this already matches plan.md Data Models' 'one struct per distinct disk type/size group' rule, no plan change needed.
- Remove the old dead fallback branches entirely (item.get('disks')/'storage'/'drives' dict/list parsing, legacy hdd_count/hdd_size_gb fields) -- none of them correspond to anything the real feed sends; per house convention, delete confirmed-dead code rather than leaving it as defensive cruft.

Acceptance criteria:
- A listing with all three disk types present in different capacities (see the mixed-disk example in the notes file: nvme:[960,960], hdd:[6000,6000]) parses into exactly 2 DiskSpec entries (NVMe count=2 capacity_gb=960, HDD count=2 capacity_gb=6000).
- A single-disk-type listing (e.g. sata:[250,250], nvme/hdd empty) parses into exactly 1 DiskSpec.

title: Genesis: hetzner-auction-dashboard Implementation
description:
## Genesis Bead
Tied to plan: docs/plan/plan.md

## Overview
Client-side dashboard for Hetzner server auction listings. A pipeline joins CPU benchmark scores onto listings and publishes a Parquet file (plus a companion unmatched-CPU report) to Cloudflare R2 via a temp-key-then-swap lifecycle; a static browser frontend on Cloudflare Pages using DuckDB-WASM does search/filter/sort only. The benchmark join itself is the core differentiator.

## Progress
- [x] Phase 1: Pipeline -- fetch Hetzner auction data, define raw schema
- [x] Phase 2: Benchmark reference table + CPU-name matching/override system + unmatched-CPU reporting
- [x] Phase 3: Cost-metric computation + Parquet writer
- [x] Phase 4: R2 bucket + API token + refresh-loop Deployment via declarative-config
- [x] Phase 5: Client dashboard -- DuckDB-WASM wiring + search/filter UI
- [x] Phase 6: Deploy pipeline to a Rackspace Spot cluster via GitOps; wire up Cloudflare Pages for web/

v1.1 additions (had-4ct, had-1vp, had-33l, had-39b, had-2ua) and v2/Future Candidates are tracked separately and do not block this genesis bead -- they are explicitly non-blocking per the plan.

title: Fetcher: switch to live_data_sb.json endpoint, parse real nested schema
description:
Phase 1's fetcher (pipeline/src/pipeline/fetcher.py) was built against an assumed Robot API schema that doesn't match reality. Full corrected endpoint + field mapping documented in docs/notes/hetzner-live-feed-schema-2026-08-06.md -- read it first, it has a live example payload and an exact field-by-field mapping table.

Changes needed in HetznerAuctionFetcher:
- base_url/endpoint: replace the two current attempts (robot.hetzner.com/order/server_market/product, /wird/json.pl) with a single GET to https://www.hetzner.com/_resources/app/data/app/live_data_sb.json (public, unauthenticated, full URL -- not a path suffix on a base_url).
- _parse_response: the existing "server" key detection already matches the real envelope ({server, filter, serverCount}) -- no change needed there.
- _parse_listing_item: rewrite to read the nested Hardware/Prices/Details structure per the mapping table in the notes file -- listing_id<-Id, cpu_raw<-Hardware.CPU.Name, ram_gb<-Hardware.RAM.Size, ram_ecc<-Hardware.RAM.ecc, datacenter<-Details.Datacenter.Name (location stays derived via the existing _extract_location_from_dc helper, unchanged), uplink_speed<-Details.Bandwidth, price_base<-round(Prices.monthly.EUR*100), price_setup_fee<-round(Prices.setup.EUR*100), available_from<-always None (not present in this feed, see Data Models note in plan.md).
- _parse_price_cents can be simplified: prices always arrive as plain EUR floats/ints now, never "euro-sign NN.NN" strings -- but don't break the existing numeric-EUR-float behavior.
- Disk parsing is a separate bead -- leave _parse_disks alone here even though it's currently wrong too.

Acceptance criteria:
- Fetcher fetches the real live endpoint end-to-end (the existing pytest.mark.integration TestRealHetznerAPI.test_fetch_real_data test, unskipped) and returns more than 0 RawListing objects with non-empty cpu_raw, positive ram_gb, and positive price_base.
- available_from is None on every parsed listing.

title: Rewrite pipeline/tests/test_fetcher.py fixtures for the real live_data_sb.json shape
description:
pipeline/tests/test_fetcher.py's sample_hetzner_response fixture and every dependent assertion are built against the old wrong flat schema (item.get('cpu'), string prices like 'euro-sign19.99', a flat disks list, an available_from timestamp). Once the fetcher rewrite beads land, none of that matches real behavior. Full real schema + a multi-disk-type example in docs/notes/hetzner-live-feed-schema-2026-08-06.md.

Changes needed:
- Replace sample_hetzner_response with real nested-schema examples (Id/Hardware/Prices/Details), covering: a single-disk-type listing, a mixed nvme+sata+hdd listing, and an ecc=true case.
- Update every assertion that references old flat fields/behavior: available_from must assert None (not a timestamp), price assertions must reflect Prices.monthly.EUR -> cents conversion (not string parsing), disk assertions must reflect the new grouped-by-capacity DiskSpec output.
- TestPriceParsing's parametrized string-format cases test a code path that no longer exists once _parse_price_cents is simplified (blocking bead) -- drop those cases, keep only the numeric-EUR-float cases.
- TestDiskParsing's dict/legacy-field test cases test the dead code removed by the disk-parsing bead -- replace with cases against the real Hardware.Storage.Details shape.
- Keep the EC-1 (empty response) and EC-2 (unrecognized schema) tests as-is -- the {server:[...]} envelope-level detection didn't change.

Acceptance criteria:
- Full pipeline/tests/test_fetcher.py suite passes against the rewritten fetcher.py.
- The existing pytest.mark.integration TestRealHetznerAPI.test_fetch_real_data test passes unskipped against the real endpoint (not just the mocked unit tests).

title: Compute the 4 derived cost metrics
description: price_effective_monthly (= price_base + price_setup_fee, full-value non-amortized), price_per_benchmark_point_single, price_per_benchmark_point_multi, price_per_gb_ram, price_per_tb_disk. NULL benchmark-point metrics when benchmark_matched = false, never a divide-by-zero or fallback estimate. Tested against a fixture set including zero and non-zero setup fee, and one unmatched listing.
